test_title: PYST 51: RRB Group D - GA (Held On: 19 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which other Bill related to Waqf matters also received Presidential assent in 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mussalman Wakf (Repeal) Bill**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mussalman Wakf (Repeal) Bill, 2025**, was introduced to formally repeal the **Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923**, a colonial-era legislation that had become redundant following the enactment of more comprehensive laws.
 
• This Bill received the **Presidential assent** in **January 2025**, following its passage in both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha** during the legislative sessions focusing on **Waqf reforms**.
 
• The primary objective of this repeal was to remove the **obsolete 1923 Act** from the statute books, as its provisions regarding the submission of accounts by **Mutawallis** were already covered under the **Waqf Act, 1995**.
 
• The repeal process was carried out alongside the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024**, which sought to bring significant transparency and accountability to the management of **Waqf properties** across **India**.
 
• The **Ministry of Minority Affairs** spearheaded these legislative changes to streamline the administration of religious endowments and ensure better utilization of land for community welfare. ***Hence, the correct answer is Mussalman Wakf (Repeal) Bill.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Waqf Act, 1995:**

 
 
• This is the principal legislation governing **Waqf** in **India**. It provides for the establishment of **State Waqf Boards** and the **Central Waqf Council**.
 
• The **2024-2025 reforms** proposed renaming this act to the **Unified Waqf Management, Empowerment, Efficiency and Development Act**.
 
• The Act defines **Waqf** as the permanent dedication of any movable or immovable property for purposes recognized by **Muslim Law** as pious, religious, or charitable.
 
 
 
• **Waqf Boards and Governance:**
 
 
• Every **State** in **India** has a **Waqf Board**, which is a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal.
 
• The **Mutawalli** is the person who manages the **Waqf property**, but they are overseen by the **State Waqf Board** to prevent mismanagement.
 
• The new amendments aim to include **Muslim women** and **non-Muslims** in these boards to increase diversity and professional oversight.
 
 
 
• **The Mussalman Wakf Act, 1923:**
 
 
• This **British-era** law was limited in scope, focusing mainly on the obligation of managers to furnish statements of particulars and accounts to the **District Court**.
 
• Because the **1995 Act** provided a much more robust mechanism for audits and judicial oversight through **Waqf Tribunals**, the **1923 Act** was no longer necessary.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC):**

 
 
• A **31-member JPC**, chaired by **Jagdambika Pal**, was constituted in **2024** to examine the **Waqf (Amendment) Bill** and related matters before they were finalized in **2025**.
 
• The committee held several meetings across **India**, including locations like **Mumbai**, **Ahmedabad**, and **Delhi**, to gather feedback from stakeholders, including **All India Muslim Personal Law Board** and various **Sufi** organizations.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the 2025 Reform Era:**
 
 
• **Digitization**: A centralized portal (**WAMSI**) is being enhanced to map all **Waqf properties** using **GIS technology** to prevent encroachments.
 
• **Audit Requirements**: The new reforms mandate that **Waqf** accounts must be audited by **auditors** appointed by the **State Government** or the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** in certain cases.
 
• **Tribunal Powers**: The **Waqf Tribunals** have been restructured to ensure that disputes regarding **property titles** are settled within a stipulated **timeframe of 6 months to 1 year**.
